blocks.html: La Fortuna Fishing Guide — San Jose del Cabo
Explore La Fortuna fishing near San Jose del Cabo: wahoo, dorado, yellowfin tuna, snapper and seasonal techniques for private charters from Puerto Los Cabos.

La Fortuna is one of the fishing grounds northeast of San Jose del Cabo where anglers can explore different techniques and target species depending on the season. Historical regional reports document opportunities for wahoo, dorado, yellowfin tuna and bottom-dwelling fish, making it a useful option when planning a flexible private fishing trip.

Instead of being associated with one species all year, La Fortuna is best understood as part of a wider network of fishing grounds that includes El 25, Iman Bank, Cardon and the Gordo Banks.

The right fishing strategy depends on current bait availability, water conditions and recent fishing activity.

Where Is La Fortuna Fishing Ground?

La Fortuna is located along the Sea of Cortez fishing grounds northeast of Puerto Los Cabos Marina in San Jose del Cabo.

It is one of several areas visited when anglers search for pelagic species or work the underwater rock structures for bottom fish.

Fishing reports frequently mention La Fortuna together with neighboring locations because boats may cover several productive areas during a single outing rather than remain at one spot.

Its location makes it part of the broader fishing experience available from San Jose del Cabo.

What Fish Can You Catch at La Fortuna?

Wahoo — One of La Fortuna's Most Interesting Opportunities

Wahoo are among the most notable species documented around La Fortuna and neighboring grounds.

A September 2025 regional report recorded wahoo activity around La Fortuna, El 25 and Iman Bank. Most reported fish averaged approximately 25 pounds, with some reaching 40–45 pounds.

Trolling deep-diving lures produced strikes during that reporting period.

Additional wahoo were reported around La Fortuna, El 25 and Cardon in January 2026.

These historical observations show that wahoo can be encountered in different parts of the year. They do not establish a guaranteed season or daily catch rate.

Dorado — Opportunities While Covering Water

Dorado, also known as mahi-mahi, are another species associated with La Fortuna.

During January 2026, regional reports described dorado weighing approximately 15–25 pounds across the La Fortuna, Cardon and Punta Gorda area.

In late March 2026, the broader fishing grounds around Iman, El 25, La Fortuna and Inner Gordo produced reports of larger dorado in the 25–40-pound range.

Trolling lures, rigged ballyhoo and live bait were among the approaches described.

Dorado activity can change quickly, so finding feeding fish and suitable ocean conditions is essential.

Yellowfin Tuna — Variable Fishing Opportunities

Yellowfin tuna have also been reported around La Fortuna and nearby waters.

For example, a January 2026 regional report described tuna averaging approximately 5–10 pounds around the La Fortuna, Cardon and Punta Gorda area, with occasional fish in the 30–40-pound range.

These fish responded to live caballito, sardines and strips of squid.

The presence of tuna does not necessarily mean that La Fortuna will be the best location on a particular day. More consistent tuna opportunities may be reported at other nearby banks, depending on current conditions.

Snapper, Grouper and Amberjack

La Fortuna also offers access to rocky fishing structure associated with bottom-dwelling species.

Historical reports from September 2025 and March 2026 describe mixed bottom-fishing opportunities around La Fortuna and neighboring high spots.

Reported species included several types of snapper, grouper and amberjack.

Fishing techniques included drifting cut bait over rocky structure and using jigs.

Bottom fishing may be a useful alternative when the wahoo or tuna bite is slow.

Fishing Techniques Used Around La Fortuna

The fishing technique should match the conditions and the intended species.

  • Trolling diving lures: Used when targeting wahoo.

  • Trolling rigged ballyhoo: Can produce encounters with wahoo, dorado and other pelagic species.

  • Live-bait fishing: Caballito and sardines have been used for yellowfin tuna and dorado.

  • Drifting cut bait: An option for bottom-associated species around rocky structure.

  • Jigging: Used when exploring deeper structure for amberjack, grouper and snapper.

Not every technique will be productive on every outing. Strong current, limited bait availability and changing fish activity can affect results.

When Is La Fortuna Worth Fishing?

La Fortuna is worth considering when recent reports indicate wahoo or dorado activity along the northeastern fishing grounds.

It may also fit an outing that combines trolling with opportunities to explore bottom structure.

Historical examples from January, March and September demonstrate that the area has produced different species across the calendar.

However, a historical catch should never be interpreted as a prediction for an upcoming trip.

La Fortuna vs. Other Fishing Grounds

La Fortuna can be considered alongside several nearby areas.

El 25 has documented yellowfin tuna, wahoo and mixed bottom-fishing opportunities.

Iman Bank has a longer record of yellowfin tuna reports and varied bottom-fishing activity.

Vinorama has frequently attracted anglers concentrating on yellowfin tuna.

The best choice depends on which species you want to target and the conditions on the day of departure.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is La Fortuna a good fishing spot for wahoo?

Historical regional reports document wahoo catches around La Fortuna and neighboring banks. Results vary with bait, water conditions and fish activity.

Can you catch tuna at La Fortuna?

Yes. Regional reports include yellowfin tuna around La Fortuna and adjacent grounds, although other banks may be more productive on particular days.

Can I fish La Fortuna on a private charter from San Jose del Cabo?

La Fortuna is among the fishing grounds that may be considered on private charters departing from Puerto Los Cabos Marina, subject to trip duration, sea conditions and the chosen fishing plan.
